claims.text: A combination of computational thermodynamics and machine learning can accurately predict the melting temperature and thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The initial high-entropy alloys are solid at room temperature.
Existing high-entropy-alloy data are available for model training.
The computational methods can be validated against experimental results.
Atomic arrangement in high-entropy alloys influences their melting behavior.
Atomic interactions in high-entropy alloys influence their thermodynamic properties.
Machine-learning models can identify data patterns correlated with melting temperature and other thermodynamic properties.
Patterns based on alloy composition and structure permit prediction of melting temperature and thermodynamic properties.
The approach will accurately predict melting temperature for a wide range of high-entropy alloys.
The approach will accurately predict enthalpy and entropy of fusion for a wide range of high-entropy alloys.
The approach will accurately predict other thermodynamic properties for a wide range of high-entropy alloys.
Current methods rely heavily on experimental measurements.
Experimental measurements of these properties can be time-consuming and resource-intensive.
The proposed approach may not be directly applicable to material classes other than high-entropy alloys.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality and quantity of machine-learning training data.
